topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Genetic origins and conditions of cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations produce cancer through clonal evolution, depending on cellular susceptibility and a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer occurrence alongside chance and inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma to illustrate the cooperation of infectious and genetic events.

topics.label: DNA damage mechanisms of environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens cause DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on biological processing and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion before tumours develop.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the tissue context and developmental state, then consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence can establish carcinogenic exposure or activity and why that evidence has limitations.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing reviews the lecture’s conclusions and frames their practical significance as everyday risk–benefit decisions.
